A shows the topography of a six-layer FePt feature made by stamping method 1, and B shows crossed FePt@SiO2 lines made by method 2. general_background.title: Heating and precursor conversion
general_background.summary: As a mixture is heated, precursor conversion and particle growth can change at different rates. Different activation barriers can make these rates change differently as temperature rises, allowing nucleation and growth to overlap.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Carboxylic-acid and carboxylate ligands
general_background.summary: Carboxylic acids and carboxylates can associate with metal-containing surfaces and solution species through their oxygen groups. The hydrocarbon part of a long-chain ligand can favour dispersion in a compatible solvent, while acid-base equilibria influence how its head group associates.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications

general_background.title: Amine coordination
general_background.summary: An amine nitrogen can donate electron density to suitable solution species or surface sites. Donation from the nitrogen lone pair and competition with other ligands can change precursor speciation and surface association.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
